beats.name: hook
beats.said: A man sneaks into a family's house nightly and shifts everything one inch left.
beats.shown: Masked burglar in garden climbs AC unit, sill, then pushes armchair; tape measure at the end.

beats.name: setup
beats.said: Nobody notices at first; by week's end the fridge blocks the door and dad doubts himself, so police are called.
beats.shown: Dad and cat in living room, then kitchen with fridge shoved to the back door, dad sweating.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: Officer mocks the complaint about an inch of furniture and laughs all the way to his car.
beats.shown: Smug officer close-up with half-lidded eyes, then circular street view of patrol car.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: They lock up, yet things keep creeping; bed meets wall; daughter hears sliding at 3 a.m.
beats.shown: Night living room, top-down bed shot, girl under quilt with bunny clock, low floor pan to cat.

beats.name: twist
beats.said: Dad stakes out on the couch with a bat, and wakes to find himself moved.
beats.shown: Dad with headlamp, lantern, bat on couch; then couch leg and slippers close-ups.

beats.name: payoff
beats.said: By month's end the couch is mid-room; the family sells at half price, to the buyer.
beats.shown: Wide living room with furniture shifted, sale sign on lawn, buyer in beanie and beard.

beats.name: ending
beats.said: He had sold them the house earlier, kept a key, and bought it back cheap.
beats.shown: Burglar with key, family photo SOLD sign, then burglar on couch with cat and sold sign.

hook.first_frame: Night garden: masked black round-headed burglar walks on stepping stones past a bush, pumpkin and AC unit by a blue clapboard house.

story.real_fact_core: Slow, tiny changes go unnoticed, so a former owner who kept a key can drive a family out and buy the house back cheap.
